Below is a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* edit that tightens up the keyword‐matching regex so that `infer`, `type`, etc. only match as *whole words* (i.e. followed by a word boundary) and will no longer highlight inside `inference` or `typeDefs`.

```javascript
### components/prism-typescript.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    // keywords that have to be followed by an identifier
    // eslint-disable-next-line regexp/no-dupe-characters-character-class
    /\b(?:asserts|infer|interface|module|namespace|type)(?!\s*[^\\s_${}*a-zA-Z\\xA0-\\uFFFF])/
=======
    // keywords that have to be followed by an identifier
    // eslint-disable-next-line regexp/no-dupe-characters-character-class
    /\b(?:asserts|infer|interface|module|namespace|type)\b/
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation:

- We replace the complex negative‐lookahead that was intended to block alphabetic continuations with a simple `\b` at the end, so only the *complete* token `infer`, `type`, etc. will be matched.
- This preserves highlighting of `const` and other TypeScript keywords, but stops partial matches like the “infer” inside “inference.”
